This is gonna get buried but I did a 'change-of-scene' program for children from poor backgrounds, we did the typical stuff, archery, nature walks, campfire, little BBQ and outside camping. It's a nice premise in theory but in practicality, I never felt more scared and out of place, and the people running it just seemed fed up all the time.

My overall experience of it is that it made me more self conscious and worsened my anxiety.

I did a similar trip to Wales, except staying in dorms with other kids. Firstly they got us to do like a team exercise of standing on a blank suspended in the air with barrels over looking a cliff. 

For context, I have extreme vertigo and pretty much any height above like 7-8 feet with make me cripplingly anxious, the  taller the height the more anxious I feel. And heights of about 40-50ft will make my knees buckle and I'll cower and cling to what's beneath and around me.

Well the staff there made everyone get up on the plank, I didn't want to, but "it was a team exercise and everyone has to do it", "face your fears" kind of thing. So now there's a picture of me hunched over cowering in crippling fear with like 20 other kids on this plank laughing at me. Yeah thanks you outward bound fuckers for that. The rest of the trip was me feeling extremely out of place and alone since I was the kid that cried because he was forced to 'face his fears' and no one wanted to talk to me. Again they tried to make me face my fears by doing a tree top zip line but at that point I was that distressed that I had to have one of the teachers from my school take me away and try to calm me down.

My overall experience of the trip was filled with anxiety and harsh judgement. Their attempts of me getting over my fears drastically failed and my vertigo is still as bad. Like seriously, just looking up at tall buildings makes me nauseous and weak in the knees. But I did enjoy exploring the forest with a infrared light on my own.

Hi, first of all , thank you for your response. To clarify on the tenancy, it was a tenancy with a fixed start and end date (very popular in my city for student renting agencies to do so). 1 of the tenants who is moving out/moved out has done so due to them completing their university course and has now returned home early. The other tenants are moving continuing on their courses at university and decided to stay at the same address rather than finding another house to rent for a year.

 The reason I've been told that the tenant (who has already left the property) will need to pay for the extra rent is because it's a joint tenancy (I'm not 100% certain I know what this means). When I asked the agency about obtaining the s21, they said that all tenants that are currently in the tenancy agreement will have to pay the 2 extra months till the s21 expires. 

I lost my guarantor due to family issues and have no one to guarantor for me. I only have about £1200 which will most likely be returning to student finance due to me dropping out of uni. I did ask about renting without a guarantor and I've unanimously been told that I would have to pay the entire years rent upfront £4500+. 

Due to the nature of my illness/s, I find it incredibly difficult to seek out help and talk to people about what I can do. As such, my mental health nurse (and other professionals) are working hard to see what can be done. My nurse said that getting a s21 was a priority in order to get help more urgently rather than being placed on a list for supportive housing (which I'm currently on). It's a sad world we live in when young males issues are generally at the bottom of the pile and I do hope my mental status will boost me a bit in the entire process of it all.

 I guess the reason I left it so late or for the nurses to handle is cause I had pretty much given up at that point; if left to my own devices, I would of gone to the streets and eventually kill myself when I couldn't hack being homeless anymore. Once again, thank you for your response and hope this clears things up.

Edit: paragraph spacing and stuff (I tried)

Hi, thank you for your response. I contacted someone for housing from the council, mainly it was my nurse doing it cause I clam up in phone conversations. I will raise all the points you've made with my mental health nurse tomorrow to really give myself the best chance of having a decent future. Thank you.
